overview.text: The OCA translates Hodegetria as She who leads the way. Its account identifies the Smolensk icon with a particular history of transfer, veneration and later copies; the iconographic title also applies to a wider family of images.

blocks.text: The pictured example is Dionysius’s Hodegetria, catalogued as a work of 1482 in the Russian Museum. Mary holds Christ and extends her hand toward him. This specific later painted example is distinguished from the earlier icon described in the Smolensk tradition.

blocks.text: The OCA presents the attribution to Saint Luke as Church Tradition. It describes the Byzantine princess Anna bringing the icon when she married Prince Vsevolod in 1046, and Vladimir Monomachos subsequently placing it in Smolensk’s Dormition cathedral at the beginning of the twelfth century.
